headline: Sam Altman meets Samsung leadership to secure more RAM for AI data centers
summary: OpenAI CEO seeks to boost memory capacity amid soaring demand and critical shortages impacting AI infrastructure.
details: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman met with around 50 senior executives from Samsung in South Korea to discuss strengthening their partnership on global AI infrastructure, particularly concerning memory semiconductors for OpenAI's Stargate project.

The meeting comes as the demand for AI data centers intensifies, leading to critical shortages of High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), a specialized DRAM crucial for AI devices. Samsung and SK Hynix currently control approximately 83% of the global HBM revenue.

Altman has previously commented on the underutilization of DRAM in personal computers, suggesting data centers could share resources more intensively across AI workloads. This statement drew criticism given OpenAI's reliance on centralized computing.

While Samsung emphasized future business opportunities and AI transformation, no new memory supply agreement was officially announced. Altman reportedly presented Samsung's AI Center head with an OpenAI Codex Micro Keyboard.

The global DRAM market is projected to see significant revenue jumps, with Trendforce estimating a 1-2% shortfall in supply versus demand this year, a gap expected to widen. Experts warn the shortage could persist until 2028.

headline_marked: Lenovo USB Drive [[Not Encrypted]] Despite Fingerprint Security
headline: Lenovo USB Drive Not Encrypted Despite Fingerprint Security
summary: A Lenovo ThinkPlus FU100 USB drive, marketed as AES-256 encrypted, was found to contain only a plain SD card. The fingerprint reader merely enabled the connection, offering no actual data protection.
details: Security researcher Xusheng Li discovered that the Lenovo ThinkPlus FU100 fingerprint USB drive, advertised with AES-256 encryption, is essentially just an SD card in a decorative case. The fingerprint scanner's sole function is to activate the USB connection, with no data on the card being encrypted.

Li stated that the FU100 is "just an SD card in a fancy case," making its data trivially accessible to anyone with physical possession. This finding highlights how "hardware security" claims can sometimes be purely marketing, a recurring issue with storage devices.

Lenovo has issued a firmware update for the FU100, FU200, TU800 drives, and TSD303 SSD, requiring users to contact a China service line for replacements or on-site upgrades. The company advises backing up and wiping data before sending devices in, causing significant inconvenience.

Further analysis revealed a flaw in Lenovo's TSD303 external SSD, where the password was transmitted in plain text over USB. While a later fix improved security, the initial attempts were vulnerable. The same development kit used for these drives was found to have vulnerabilities in nine other devices from various vendors.

The research also demonstrated the increasing role of AI in security analysis. AI tools like OpenAI's Codex assisted in reverse-engineering protection schemes, finding hardcoded keys and passwords in diagnostic logs, and even decrypting test files without user passwords.
